log.msg: usage refresh SKIPPED — the brief's fence names only ux/page.js, ux/*/page.js, ux/ux.css, CardAnswer.js (one line if needed), the task dir, and ai/page.js children: — not ai/usage.json/usage.jsonl, so per new-task skill I left the mastermind's snapshot alone.

root cause of "single page with a bunch of tabs": ux/page.js was a Doc, and Doc.bar() puts every declared child (all 10 modules) into the top TAB strip, not a wall — that's the tab overflow the owner saw. Doc also derives Overview/API/Docs/Files as extra children in the same Map, which is why ux/page.js carried leaf:true (core/Page/doc/data-children.md): without it, ux/Tree/Tree.js's node_of() would have drawn the sidebar rail branch out of ALL of them, chrome included, not just the ten modules.

decision: converted ux/page.js from Doc to a plain Page (byte-for-byte the shape /framework/styles/page.js already uses) instead of teaching Doc to suppress its own tab bar. A plain Page's children Map holds exactly the ten declared modules, nothing else — so dropping leaf:true now expands the sidebar rail to EXACTLY ten rows (proven below), where staying a Doc and only patching bar()/leaf would have expanded it to twelve (the ten plus Overview and Docs chrome), missing the brief's own "ten children" wording. Alternative rejected: keep Doc, override bar() to hide the module tabs and leave leaf:true — cheaper, but the rail still would not expand, which is deliverable 1's other explicit ask.

side effect of that decision, checked and accepted: each ux/<Module> Doc page (Auth, Wizard, ...) no longer has a Doc ancestor, so Doc.nested_in_doc() now renders them top-level (their own H1 well + a short horizontal Overview/Docs/Files tab strip) instead of a nested vertical rail. This is the SAME shape core/View, core/Page, core/Router etc. already use (their parent, core/page.js, is a plain Page too) — not a new pattern, and it actually removes the double-well bug nested_in_doc() was originally written to paper over. Screenshotted /framework/ux/Auth/ before and after; no visual break, no console error.

the two long-form docs (doc/system.md, doc/decisions.md, linked from ~15 files across ux/) needed to keep resolving without being declared children (a declared child is a wall CARD, and a doc page is not a module). Gave ux/page.js a route(name) for "doc" only, returning a stub page with no children of its own — "system"/"decisions" under it then resolve through core's OWN existing fallback (Page.child() tries <name>/page.js, then <name>.md — the second one hits doc/system.md and doc/decisions.md directly, the same mechanism any bare .md sibling page already uses site-wide). Proved /framework/ux/doc/system/ and /framework/ux/doc/decisions/ both render their full content correctly, and that route() never puts "doc" in the sidebar unless someone actually visits it (it shows up as a one-off "UX Docs" row only after that).

finding, not a bug I introduced: those two doc/ pages each log one browser-level "Failed to load resource: 404" console line, because core/Page.child()'s own two-step probe (try <name>/page.js first, THEN <name>.md) makes a real failing network request for the page.js half before falling through — Page.load() catches that failure in JS (Page.missing() suppresses its own console.error) but Chrome still logs the raw failed fetch itself. Same cosmetic noise on every bare-.md page site-wide, not specific to this page. My four required proof shots (index, one module page, rail expanded, a flag pressed) never touch this fallback path — those are genuinely 0 console errors, checked.

- [The index](/framework/ux/) — ten live-thumbnail cards, hover one to flag it
- [`ux/page.js`](/framework/ux/page.js) (was a `Doc`, now a plain `Page` — no tab bar, no Overview/Docs chrome mixed into the wall or the rail) · [`ux/ux.css`](/framework/ux/ux.css) (new) · [`ux/readme.md`](/framework/ux/readme.md)
- Card fix, measured real (not framework.css's generic numbers) — button-to-button gap was `gap: normal` (0px, a broken self-referencing `--gap` hack) on **both** cards; now `.gap-35`, 5.26px at 1280 / 15.12px at 3440. Card padding was `.pad` (the page-region token — 15px default / 7.5px compact at 1280, 18px / 9px at 3440, i.e. compact was starving); now `.card` (`--pad-card`, floor-protected) — 16px on both, at both widths.
- Reject flag — hover a card, press the flag, type one line, it lands on `ai/verdicts.jsonl` as an `improve` through the same `card_say` rpc the AI board uses, and a quiet marker stays on the card. Proved end to end (screenshot + the real jsonl line, in the log).
